summary: Coronado NF ground cabin on Buena Vista Peak, AZ: 1935 build, NRHP 1988, destroyed by the June 2011 Horseshoe II fire; only the foundation is described today.

facts.design: 14-by-14-foot wood-frame L-4 ground cabin with a roof-catch cistern
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the June 2011 Horseshoe II fire; the Register's field reads 'Removed June 2011'; the sources describe only the foundation

events.note: Constructed in 1935; the Register and Forest Lookouts credit a Civilian Conservation Corps crew, which Wikipedia calls a hypothesis
June 1946: smoke from a fire two miles away completely enveloped the station; William J. Fry was the lookout

Listed on the National Register as No. 87002463, part of the National Forest Fire Lookouts in the Southwestern Region multiple-property listing; NPS weekly list dates it January 28, 1988, Wikipedia July 28, 1988
Registered December 30, 1996 as US 218, AZ 12; nominated by Dave Lorenz, Arizona Registrar
Overrun by the Horseshoe Two (Horseshoe II, Horseshoe 2) Fire in early June 2011 and destroyed; the Register's field reads Removed June 2011
Registered March 14, 2014 as US 1547, AZ 1; nominated by James Nuti

corrections.why: 4.3 m is about 14 feet, which is the cabin's 14-by-14-foot floor footprint, not a height. No source gives a height for this ground cabin.

The Register's 'Removed' field says June 2011, but its own description and the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register say the Horseshoe II fire destroyed the lookout. The event should be destroyed, not removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1946 newspaper item quoted by Forest Lookouts calls the lookout's peak Barefoot peak; Wikipedia places the complex on Buena Vista Peak. The story uses Buena Vista Peak and attributes the other spelling to the 1946 item.
The NPS weekly list gives January 28, 1988 (01/28/88); Wikipedia gives July 28, 1988. The story gives both and does not pick one.
The Register and Forest Lookouts credit the Civilian Conservation Corps with building it in 1935; Wikipedia says that is a hypothesis marked citation needed. The story reports both.
The Register writes Horseshoe II, Forest Lookouts writes Horseshoe Two, and Wikipedia writes Horseshoe 2. All describe the June 2011 fire that overran the lookout.

sources.title: National Register of Historic Places Weekly List, January to September 1988

notes_for_editor: Core facts agree across four sources: 1935 build, the June 2011 fire loss, and the foundation. Open points: the NRHP date (NPS list vs Wikipedia), and the CCC builder credit, which Wikipedia flags as unverified. The Wikipedia page cites an Arizona Daily Star article of July 9, 2011 that was not read. A search snippet mentioned a 1938 construction date on Living New Deal; that page was not read, so it is not used. The 1946 Fry clipping is the only staffing evidence; no source says when the lookout was last staffed. Whether the foundation can be visited is not described in any source read. The brief's height_m of 4.3 is the footprint misread; corrected above.
